pairs.evidence: src/lib/standard/maintain.ts:133 The `note` writer's exclusive create is keyed on id plus slug, so two concurrent writers with different text both succeed under the same numeric `id`, and because `markSuperseded` matches on `entryId` a later `supersedes` of that id retires both entries.

techniques.evidence: src/lib/standard/maintain.ts:133 Technique requires a create-if-absent that fails when the IDENTITY is taken; the 'wx' create here covers id+slug (the comment at line 129 says so), so differing slugs mint duplicate ids. standard.test.ts:290 pins only the wx flag and EEXIST retry.

src/lib/standard/memory.ts:12 The seeded store declares no cap, retention horizon, demotion or reaper for any kind, so it only grows; the caps in repo-memory-mirror.ts bound mirrored rows, not this store.

src/lib/standard/maintain.ts:134 `note` commits decisions and conventions directly with no judgment pass, no confidence and no episode provenance (only a trailing `(at sha)`), and hard-codes `supersedes: null`, so the tool door cannot supersede. Supersede-not-edit, failed-approach as a kind and an unrecognized-kind default are realized (memory.ts:44, :26; memory-read.ts:106).

src/lib/standard/memory-read.ts:162 The cut is flagged only as a ledger field (`truncated`, then skipReason); memoryBody() feeds the cut body to OrgMemory with no in-band notice. `refs` (line 88) and scalars (line 76) are also capped silently. Unreadable entries are counted properly (line 187).

src/lib/standard/memory.ts:30 Links sit beside the body as the technique wants, but agents type target ids freely and nothing resolves them: doctor.ts only checks the directory exists (line 171), although spec.ts:196 lists 'memory entries are well-formed' under what doctor checks.

src/lib/standard/memory.ts:41 Supersedence is recorded only on the successor, the read norm neither filters nor labels predecessors, and an old entry carries no marker that it is dead. No stale-served measure exists. Applies to direct repo readers; the OrgMemory mirror does archive predecessors.

src/lib/standard/memory-read.ts:187 The parser never throws, counts unreadable entries by cause rather than reading them as absent, and separates malformed from empty; the write path appends a new file and never rewrites existing entries (maintain.ts:136).
src/lib/standard/memory-read.ts:13 This context has no model-driven selector or load-by-id path; it parses documents only.
src/lib/standard/memory-read.ts:38 No distillation pass grounds relative time here; `note` stamps at capture and the reader keeps the date verbatim.

src/lib/standard/memory.ts:20 The format fixes a one-fact grain, but this context imposes no read budget or retriever, and the directory of slugged filenames is itself a surveyable list, so the technique's reach trade does not arise.

pairs.registryProposal: episodic-capture could name the suffixed-filename form as a failure of atomic allocation: an exclusive create on `<id>-<slug>` satisfies a check for an exclusive-create flag while still minting duplicate ids, because the claimed name is not the identity.
